title: Repair hypothesis-parser MCP
chat: User: "fix the mcp tool by installing the correct version of openai".
decision: Do NOT install openai — it was never missing.
why: The bare CLI has no PEP-723 header so `uv run` gave it a minimal env; the MCP server's hypothesis_mcp.py DOES declare openai>=1.40 and resolved openai 3.16.0. Real cause: mcp.json passed the literal string ${OPENAI_API_KEY}, which nothing expands, so _resolve_api_key() fell back to placeholder 'ac.jdoe'.
outcome: Probe proved it: user='avasan'->'OK', user='ac.jdoe'->ACCESS DENIED (returned as HTTP 200 text). Set literal env in mcp.json; tools live.

title: Stages 1-3: hypothesis -> search spec
chat: Decompose the NFKB/HepB hypothesis into testable components.
why: The skill forbids inferring direction, but the hypothesis text literally says 'high ... poor', so the direction is read, not invented. Flagged to the user as an open gate.

title: ImmPort study search
chat: Find HepB vaccine studies matching the spec.
decision: Search on intervention terms only (require: intervention).
why: ImmPort ANDs all words in a query; ORing predictor terms like 'inflammation' would drag in unrelated studies without adding HepB specificity.
outcome: 11 accessions: SDY89, SDY690, SDY1328, SDY816, SDY299, SDY2312, SDY1538, SDY2584, SDY671, SDY674, SDY3271.

title: Readiness gate on GEO linkage
chat: Which of the 11 are actually analysable?
decision: Gate BEFORE downloading, on presence of expsample_public_repository.txt.
why: A study with no GEO linkage can never yield an expression matrix; downloading it wastes time and pollutes the cache. Cheaper to test the linkage table than to discover the gap later.
outcome: 5/11 ready (SDY1328, SDY299, SDY2312, SDY1538, SDY2584). Correctly discarded the 3 transplant false positives (SDY671/674/3271) plus SDY89/690/816.

title: Fetch + parse ImmPort archives
chat: Pull the Tab archives for the 5 ready studies.
decision: Filter to *_Tab.zip rather than capping file count.
why: ImmPort lists flow-cytometry result files first, so a bare max_files cap never reaches the small Tab archive that holds subject/ELISA tables.
outcome: 5/5 archives fetched; combined manifest 32,677 rows. SDY1328 = 174 subjects, microarray + ELISA.

title: Choose the analysable cohort
chat: Which study can actually test the hypothesis?
decision: Analyse SDY1328 alone; do not pool studies.
why: SDY1328 was the ONLY HepB study with a resolved GEO series (GSE65834 pre-vax + GSE125860 post-vax). The other four returned 'review' — Nanostring/mass-spec/methylation with no linked matrix. It is also the best on merit: 174 subjects, single arm, day-0 microarray AND anti-HBs ELISA.
outcome: Target unit SDY1328/EXP16735/GSE65834_GPL15048 — 169 baseline samples x 60,607 probes.

title: GEO download + parse
chat: Retrieve and parse the series matrices.
decision: On MCP timeout, run the SAME module the server wraps — not a hand-rolled downloader.
why: LOOM.global.md forbids substituting replacement code. The timeout was the response, not the job: files were already on disk. Re-running the identical module under the server's own .venv (which pins GEOparse 2.0.4) preserved provenance and wrote the manifest the next stage needs.
outcome: 2/2 series cached+validated; 8/11 units parsed; list_analysis_units now works (it had been failing on the missing manifest).

title: Probe mapping and outcome join
chat: Build one row per subject: baseline NF-kB + anti-HBs.
decision: Average multiple probes per gene; take outcome from ImmPort VALUE_PREFERRED.
why: RELA has 4 probes and REL 2; picking one arbitrarily is a hidden researcher degree of freedom, so all probes for a gene are averaged. VALUE_PREFERRED was an explicit standing user instruction.
outcome: 165 subjects with complete data. All 5 genes present on the platform; NFKB1 uniquely mapped.

title: Cross-validate the outcome variable
chat: Is ImmPort's '7 Days' really the post-vaccination titer?
planned: compare ImmPort ELISA against GEO sample characteristics
called: bash: parse series-matrix characteristics_ch1 and diff vs ImmPort
decision: Treat the ImmPort day-7 record as the study's final post-vax reading.
why: Day 7 would be implausibly early for an antibody response, which threatened the whole analysis. Two INDEPENDENT sources settle it — ImmPort ELISA and GEO metadata agreed exactly on 165/165 subjects, 0 mismatches.
outcome: Outcome validated; 58 responders (>=10 mIU/mL) vs 107 non-responders.

title: Pre-specified statistical test
decision: Two-sided, BH over exactly 5 genes, NFKB1 pre-declared primary.
why: One pre-specified primary prevents laundering 5 tests into a 'finding'. Two-sided keeps a positive association detectable rather than assumed away.
outcome: All 5 negative as hypothesised; none significant. NFKB1 rho=-0.118, p=0.132, q=0.237.

title: Confounder check
chat: Cohort is elderly (25-83, mean 64.6) — could age drive this?
called: bash: partial Spearman via rank residuals
decision: Test age explicitly rather than reporting the raw rho alone.
why: Inflammaging plausibly raises baseline NF-kB AND lowers vaccine response, which would manufacture the hypothesised correlation without any causal link.
outcome: Confirmed confounding: age->titer rho=-0.209 (p=0.007), age->NFKB1 rho=+0.265 (p=0.001). Adjusted NFKB1 rho halves to -0.066 (p=0.400).

title: Verdict via frozen decision rule
decision: Count the 5 genes as ONE independent group, not five.
why: They are co-regulated subunits of one pathway in one study on one platform. Treating them as 5 confirmations would be the exact error the module warns about.
outcome: verdict=inconclusive, validate_synthesis()==[] (schema-valid). Narrative records the pre-registration and the single-group caveat.

title: Build report.html
chat: Compile a report with plots illustrating conclusions.
decision: Lead with the null and foreground age as the substantive finding.
why: The interesting result is not 'NF-kB does nothing' but 'the apparent signal is largely age'. Reporting the raw rho alone would overstate the case.
outcome: report.html 263 KB, 4 embedded plots, HTML well-formed (0 unclosed/mismatched tags).

title: Broaden to inflammation gene sets
chat: User: "Can you potentially try other genes related to inflammation to establish this relationship? Feel free to use GEO as well as ImmPort."
called: bash: probe MSigDB/Enrichr for hallmark sets
decision: Test ONE composite score per gene set, not N genes individually.
why: Sweeping a large panel after a null 5-gene test and reporting the smallest p is exactly the multiple-testing laundering the frozen-rule discipline exists to prevent. Collapsing a set to a single z-score composite gives one test and one p-value, so the result means something. Also chose the TNFa/NF-kB TARGET signature as primary because Session 13's own stated weakness was that NFKB1 mRNA is a poor proxy for NF-kB activity -- target genes measure the pathway's output.
outcome: Design approved by user. MSigDB Hallmark fetched via Enrichr (50 sets); 95-98% of each set present on GPL15048. Donor-set split (123/46) discovered -> real held-out replication.

title: Primary composite test (age-adjusted)
chat: Run the frozen primary: one age-adjusted composite vs anti-HBs.
decision: Age-adjusted is PRIMARY, not a sensitivity check.
why: Session 13 established age confounds both the predictor and the outcome. Reporting the unadjusted rho as headline would repeat the overstatement the notebook explicitly warns about.
outcome: All 4 sets negative but null. Primary TNFa/NF-kB rho_adj=-0.053, p=0.503, q=0.503 -- the WEAKEST of the four.

title: Genome-wide exploratory sweep
chat: Does anything at all predict response?
planned: age-adjusted partial Spearman for every gene
decision: Report the sweep as exploratory and interpret the NULL, not the top hit.
why: With 0 genes at q<0.05, quoting EFHC2 (p=2.3e-05, q=0.51) as a lead would be noise-mining. The informative fact is the distribution, not its minimum.
outcome: 22,115 genes; 0 at q<0.05; 990 at p<0.05 vs ~1,106 expected by chance -- BELOW null. QQ plot on the diagonal. No transcriptional signal exists in this cohort.

title: Permutation test kills the one apparent finding
chat: IFN-gamma looked enriched: 29 genes in the top 5% vs 9.8 expected.
planned: permute subject labels 2000x preserving gene-gene correlation
decision: Do not report the IFN-gamma enrichment as a finding.
why: The 9.8 'expected' assumes genes are independent draws. Pathway members are co-regulated, so that baseline is wrong and the enrichment is inflated. Permuting subject labels preserves the correlation structure and gives the honest null.
outcome: IFN-gamma p=0.058 -- NOT significant. The one result that looked like a finding dissolved under the correct test.

title: Held-out replication on donor sets
chat: Does the (null) pattern hold in an independent split?
planned: re-run all 4 composites separately in donor set 1 and 2
called: bash: replication.py using GEO 'donor set' characteristic
decision: Use the study's own donor sets as the replication split.
why: Session 13's biggest limitation was no replication. The donor-set field is an internal, pre-existing split not chosen by me, so it is not a split engineered to produce an answer.
outcome: All 4 sets sign-consistent (negative) in BOTH halves, all null (p>0.26). A stable null rather than a split-sample artefact.

title: Extend both HTML documents
chat: Fold the extension into the living documents.
decision: Keep verdict INCONCLUSIVE, but state that the grounds are now much stronger.
why: The verdict word is unchanged, yet the evidence behind it changed qualitatively: cohort-wide null, mRNA-proxy loophole closed, internally replicated. Saying only 'still inconclusive' would undersell what was learned; saying 'refuted' would overclaim.
outcome: report.html 524 KB, 8 plots, sections 10-15. synthesize()=inconclusive, validate_synthesis()==[].
